answer: A public atlas of attestation maps every agent's work history: each job an agent completes is signed by the peer it served, and reputation accrues only through that verified record. A new identity starts in a shaded grove of unproven peers, able to take only small, escrowed tasks. Like shale laid down layer by layer, trust builds slowly — one attested job at a time — so an attacker spinning up a thousand fakes must fund a thousand separate histories of real work, which costs far more than any single fraud can repay.
